headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/clipboard/MCP pathways between a browser-capable support agent and a writable coding IDE.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can use browsers, MCPs, and runtime-injected hooks; agent B has clipboard, filesystem, and MCP access. That creates a plausible path for A’s outputs or web content to reach B as trusted instructions. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent A content is copied into agent B’s clipboard or workspace files
IF a shared MCP server forwards A-generated text to B without provenance tags
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Require provenance labels on all MCP messages
Use separate workspaces per agent
Turn off auto-execute in Windsurf
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches provider auth data, session history, and project code; agent B reads and writes workspace files and uses broad network egress. A shared local filesystem or copied files could expose A’s sensitive context to B, and B can transmit that context outward. The profiles do not show hard isolation.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local workspace or config directory
IF A’s session history or auth prompts are placed into files readable by B
mitigations: Separate per-agent directories
Remove auth prompts from shared folders
Restrict B’s network egress during shared work
Rotate any exposed provider credentials
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level ACL isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem and modify git state; agent A can spawn subprocesses and uses task-scoped isolation but also requests full-permissions mode. If they operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can clobber each other. The shared-state path is explicit for B and plausible for A, so this is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or config tree
IF either agent performs git commits, rebases, or file rewrites without locking
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Pause one agent before the other writes
Disable auto-commit workflows
Use file locks for shared paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can act on files and git state, while agent A can generate support content and use browser/MCP tools. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, an error or hallucination from A can cascade into edits, commits, or external actions. No verification step is documented between them, so the unsafe default is material.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as instructions or facts
IF B is allowed to commit or execute commands based on A’s output without review
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output
Insert a verification step for citations and commands
Disable auto-execute in B
Limit A to drafting only
requires-engineering: add structured handoff validation

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles provider authentication data and session history; agent B handles source code and open files with broad network egress. The profiles do not show residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is placed into the shared workflow. This is not provably a breach, but the gap is real.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into A’s session history or B’s workspace
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared project
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review retention settings for both tools
Separate regulated and unregulated projects
Disable external network access for sensitive sessions
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
